title: Antennas, beacons and permitted signals
blurb: Antenna height and PRB-1 limits, beacon rules, what you may transmit or relay, and who sets good practice.

G1B01.why: Structures up to **200 ft** (not near a public use airport) need no FAA notice or FCC registration.
G1B01.trap: 50 and 100 ft are far too low; 250 ft is over the line.

G1B02.why: Only **one beacon per band per location** is required by rule. No beacon coordinator, and no posting requirement.
G1B02.trap: The coordination and publication options are made up.

G1B03.why: A beacon exists to **observe propagation and reception**. It is not a repeater ID or a bulletin station.

G1B04.why: **Occasional** relay of US government weather and propagation forecasts is allowed. Automatic relay by any station, encryption and unidentified tests are not.
G1B04.trap: Automatic retransmission is limited to certain station types, not any station.

G1B05.why: One-way **Morse code learning** transmissions are allowed. Unidentified tests and regular sale offers are not.
G1B05.trap: All three choices together is not correct.

G1B06.why: Local rules must **reasonably accommodate** amateur communications and be the **minimum practical** (PRB-1).
G1B06.trap: FCC priority is not absolute, and local rules are not unlimited.

G1B07.why: Abbreviations and procedural signals are allowed if they **do not obscure meaning**. Q signals are not the only ones.

G1B08.why: You may contact any country **except** those that told the ITU they object. No treaty or UN membership is needed.
G1B08.trap: A third-party agreement is for third-party traffic, not for all contacts.

G1B09.why: Automatic HF beacons go on **28.20 to 28.30 MHz** in the 10 m band.

G1B10.why: Beacon output is limited to **100 W PEP**.

G1B11.why: Where Part 97 is silent, the **FCC** decides what counts as good engineering and good amateur practice.
G1B11.trap: Not the control operator, the IEEE or the ITU.
